'''Paul Gassman''' (June 22, 1935–April 21, 1993) was an American chemist. He is best known for his research in the field of [[organic chemistry]] and his service as president of the [[American Chemical Society]] and is listed among notable alumni by the [[Cornell University]] Graduate School.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gradschool.cornell.edu/notable-alumni|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141105143721/http://gradschool.cornell.edu/notable-alumni|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 November 2014|title=Notable Alumni - Graduate School|website=gradschool.cornell.edu}}</ref>

==Biography==
Gassman was the son of Joseph Martin Gassman and Florence Marie Rautenstrauch Gassman, of German Swiss parentage.<ref name="minutes">{{cite journal |url=https://hdl.handle.net/11299/48231 |title=Minutes: Faculty Senate and University Senate: February 17, 1994: Paul G. Gassman (1935–1993)|author=<!--Not stated--> |website=University of Minnesota Digital Conservancy|date=17 February 1994 |publisher=University of Minnesota|hdl=11299/48231 |access-date=October 31, 2021}}</ref> In 1957, he graduated with a B.S. degree in chemistry from [[Canisius College]] in Buffalo, New York and received his Ph.D. in three years from Cornell University in 1960, where he studied under [[Jerrold Meinwald]].<ref name="cornell.edu">{{cite web|url=https://gradschool.cornell.edu/paul-gassman-60-chemistry|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150118042651/http://gradschool.cornell.edu/paul-gassman-60-chemistry|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 January 2015|title=Paul Gassman '60, Chemistry - Graduate School|website=gradschool.cornell.edu}}</ref> He continued at Cornell as a postdoctoral fellow before his appointment as an Assistant Professor of Chemistry at the [[Ohio State University]]. After becoming a full professor at Ohio State in 1969, Gassman brought his research to the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1974.<ref name="umn.edu">{{cite web|url=http://www1.chem.umn.edu/alumni/HistoryWeb/PDF%20WriteUps/Newsletters/1993.pdf|title=Minnesota Chemists Newsletter - Fall 1993|website=www1.chem.umn.edu}}</ref> He served as chair of its chemistry department from 1975 to 1979, and was named a Regents' Professor in 1988.<ref name="minutes"/>

==Career==
Gassman's work centered in the areas of organic reaction mechanisms (including the [[Gassman indole synthesis]]), mechanisms of catalysis (including hydrocarbon metathesis), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, cyclo-addition reactions, enzyme mechanisms, organoelectro-chemistry, carbanion chemistry, synthesis of heterocyclic molecules, oxidation of hydrocarbons, nitrenium ion chemistry, and electron-transfer reactions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scripps.edu/baran/images/grpmtgpdf/See_04_2015.pdf|title=The Career of Paul Gassman|website=www.scripps.edu}}</ref> This work helped him achieve status as an internationally recognized chemist.<ref>{{cite news|last1=harva015|accessdate=2018-03-28|title=History|url=https://chem.umn.edu/about-us/history|newspaper=Department of Chemistry|date=13 April 2016}}</ref> serving the American Chemical Society as Chairman of the Division of Organic Chemistry (1981) and eventually as [[President of the American Chemical Society]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/about/president/acspresidents.html|title=ACS Presidents, A Chronological List - American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society}}</ref> Gassman's research resulted in over 300 publications in scientific journals, 33 patents,<ref name="umn.edu"/> and 11 books.<ref name="cornell.edu"/> During his career, he advised 72 Ph.D. and 13 masters' students, along with dozens of postdoctoral fellows and a number of undergraduates.<ref name="minutes"/>

He received recognition as a [[Fulbright Scholar]] (1988), membership in both the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (1989) and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1992), and his notable awards included the Chemical Pioneers Award of the American Institute of Chemists (1990), and the National Catalyst Award of the Chemical Manufacturers Association (1990). In 1989, he was elected to the presidency of the 138,000-member American Chemical Society.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|title=Minnesota Chemist Newsletter Summer 1989|url=http://www1.chem.umn.edu/alumni/HistoryWeb/PDF%20WriteUps/Newsletters/1989.pdf}}</ref> The day he assumed office was declared "Paul Gassman Day" in Minnesota by Governor [[Arne H. Carlson]].<ref>{{cite web|title=procalamation of the governor|url=https://www.leg.state.mn.us/archive/sos/cards/pdf/proclamations_0001700474.pdf|accessdate=9 December 2016}}</ref> In his service as President of the A.C.S., Gassman said it was his mission to show “the population at large that chemistry has been extremely beneficial, that they are living longer because of chemistry, and that they are living better because of chemistry”<ref name="auto"/>

==Death==
Gassman suffered an [[aortic dissection]] at his home on the evening of April 17, 1993. Despite emergency open-heart surgery the following day, he suffered irreversible brain damage and died aged 57 on April 21 without regaining consciousness.<ref name="minutes"/> The American Chemical Society recognized his service by creating the Paul G. Gassman Distinguished Service Award,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.organicdivision.org/professional-awards/gassmanaward/|title=Paul G. Gassman Distinguished Service Award - American Chemical Society, Division of Organic Chemistry|website=Organic Division}}</ref> granted for outstanding service in the organic chemical community. Both the University of Minnesota, through the Paul G. Gassman Lectureship in Chemistry <ref>{{cite web|url=https://chem.umn.edu/news/gassman-family-creates-graduate-student-travel-fund|title=Gassman family creates graduate student travel fund|last=Anonymous|date=19 July 2011|publisher=}}</ref> and Canisius College through the Gassman Memorial Seminar Series<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.canisius.edu/chemistry/learn/gassman-seminar-series/ |title=Gassman Seminar Series &#124; Learn Outside the Classroom &#124; Chemistry &#124; Canisius College |access-date=2016-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220202723/http://www.canisius.edu/chemistry/learn/gassman-seminar-series/ |archive-date=2016-12-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> host chemistry lecture series in his honor.
